summary_plain: Moves about 9 arcseconds per hour across 21 images over 34.3 hours. Not yet checked against JPL's catalog of known asteroids and comets.

orbit.reported_orbit: The arc is too short to fix one orbit, so this is the most circular of the 240 sampled orbits that fit the detections; the clones show the range.

known_object.not_checked_reason: JPL Horizons did not answer for 2437 Amnestia (1942 RZ), the closest known object (about 37″ away in JPL's quick search).

scores.definition: Rule-based ranking score in [0, 1]: motion_consistency x snr x (1 - artifact_likelihood). It orders candidates for review. It is not a probability.

anomaly.reason_plain: Moving at 24° to the ecliptic, steeper than most objects we have tracked
anomaly.definition: Isolation Forest over motion rate, motion across the ecliptic, ecliptic latitude, distance from the Sun and infrared colour of every published object with a motion fit over 3 or more detections (not two-detection pairs or likely artifacts). It ranks how unlike the others an object is; unusual does not mean new or unexplained.

history.change: linked 21 detections over 4 visits from 2025-05-17 to 2025-05-18

disclaimer: An unmatched candidate may be an imaging artifact, a measurement error, or an object missing from the catalogs we checked. This is not a discovery claim.
